The objective of this R Markdown code is to analyse the results obtained by the single cell RNA sequencing.

```{r}
Datafolder     <- here("Data")

utils_file <- here("Rscripts","utils.R")
if (file.exists(utils_file)) source(utils_file)
```

Read in normalized data and process separately for each cell type
```{r}
nHVG <- 2000 # 2000 is usually enough to capture sub-states. (5000 HVGs might be too many for a single cell type.)
nHVG_str <- as.character(nHVG)
for (ct in c("EpiC", "kolf2")){
# for (ct in c("EpiC")){
# for (ct in c("kolf2")){
  outfile <- file.path(Data_calc, "seu_final.rds")
  seu.norm <- LoadSeuratRds(file=outfile) # it is not yet normalized, but will be
  # write out cell numbers
  table(seu.norm@meta.data$sample.names)
  
  message("Starting processing for: ", ct)
  seu.cell <- subset(seu.norm, subset = sample.names %in% grep(ct, unique(sample.names), value = TRUE))
  seu.cell <- JoinLayers(seu.cell) # before splitting, layers should be joined
  table(seu.cell@meta.data$sample.names)
  
  # rename to reflect further processing
  seu.integrated <- seu.cell
  
  ##########################################################
  # save here
  outfile <- file.path(Data_calc, paste("seu_integrated_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".rds", sep=""))
  SaveSeuratRds(seu.integrated, file=outfile)
  
  nHVG_norm <- 2000
  # SCT-normalized values for marker detection
  seu.integrated <- SCTransform(seu.integrated, 
  method = "glmGamPoi", # glmGamPoi for speed and accuracy
  variable.features.n = nHVG_norm, 
  #vars.to.regress = c("ccvar", "percent.mito"),
  #vars.to.regress = c("ccvar"),
  vars.to.regress = c("S.Score", "G2M.Score"),
  verbose = F)
  
  # quick visual check
  seu.integrated <- RunPCA(seu.integrated, verbose = F)
  
  # decide dimensions automatically
  stdevs <- seu.integrated[["pca"]]@stdev
  pct <- stdevs / sum(stdevs) * 100
  cum <- cumsum(pct)
  co1 <- which(cum > 90)[1] # 90% of total variance explained
  co2 <- sort(which((pct[1:(length(pct) - 1)] - pct[2:length(pct)]) > 0.1), decreasing = TRUE)[1] + 1 # Finds the last PC where the drop in variance is greater than 0.1%.
  selected_dims <- min(co1, co2) # We take the minimum of these two to avoid including noisy, low-variance PCs.
  # overwrite if too low!
  if (is.na(selected_dims) || selected_dims < 10) { # fallback
  selected_dims <-  10}
  print(paste(ct, "| Auto-selected Dims:", selected_dims))
  # visualise the selected elbow
  p <- ElbowPlot(seu.integrated, ndims=ceiling(1.5*selected_dims)) + 
    geom_vline(xintercept = selected_dims, color = "red")
  outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("elbow_plot_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
  ggsave(outfig, p, width=6, height = 6)
  
  seu.integrated <- RunUMAP(seu.integrated, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:selected_dims, 
                            verbose = F)
  
  # check whether cell cycle has been properly regressed out
  p1 <- DimPlot(seu.integrated, group.by = "sample.names", reduction = "umap") + ggtitle("By Sample")
  p2 <- FeaturePlot(seu.integrated, features = "S.Score", reduction = "umap") + ggtitle("S Phase Signal")
  p1 + p2
  
  seu.integrated <- FindNeighbors(object = seu.integrated, dims = 1:selected_dims)
  seu.integrated <- FindClusters(object = seu.integrated, resolution = seq(0.1, 1.2, by=0.1)) # try different resolutions
  #seu.integrated <- FindClusters(object = seu.integrated, resolution = seq(1.5, 1.8, by=0.1)) # try different resolutions
  p <- clustree::clustree(seu.integrated@meta.data[,grep("SCT_snn_res", colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data))],
                   prefix = "SCT_snn_res.")
  outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("clustree_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
  ggsave(outfig, p, width=20, height = 20)
  
  
  seu.integrated <- RunUMAP(object = seu.integrated, dims = 1:selected_dims)
  
  # save here as well
  outfile <- file.path(Data_calc, paste("seu_integrated_clusters_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".rds", sep=""))
  SaveSeuratRds(seu.integrated, file=outfile)
  
  
  res_vector <- c("SCT_snn_res.0.1", "SCT_snn_res.0.2",
                 "SCT_snn_res.0.3", "SCT_snn_res.0.4",
                "SCT_snn_res.0.5", "SCT_snn_res.0.6",
                "SCT_snn_res.0.7", "SCT_snn_res.0.8",
                "SCT_snn_res.0.9", "SCT_snn_res.1",
                "SCT_snn_res.1.1", "SCT_snn_res.1.2")
                # "SCT_snn_res.1.3", "SCT_snn_res.1.4",
                # "SCT_snn_res.1.5", "SCT_snn_res.1.6",
                # "SCT_snn_res.1.7", "SCT_snn_res.1.8")
  p <- DimPlot(seu.integrated, reduction = "umap", group.by = res_vector)
  outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("clustree_umap_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
  ggsave(outfig, p, width=20, height = 20)

  
  # Van-Haver markers - ensure genes are present
  marker_list_filtered <- lapply(marker_list, function(genes) {
    genes[genes %in% rownames(seu.integrated)]
  })
  
  # subtracting the average expression of "control genes" from the feature genes
  seu.integrated <- AddModuleScore(
      seu.integrated,
      features = marker_list_filtered,
      name     = names(marker_list_filtered),
      nbin     = 10
    )
  
  # add nice metadata columns (names of the marker_list_filtered list plus a "1" suffix)
  new_cols <- grep(paste0("(", paste(names(marker_list_filtered), collapse="|"), ")\\d+"), 
               colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data), value = TRUE)
  marker_names <- gsub("\\d+$", "", new_cols)
  names(marker_names) <- new_cols
  colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data)[colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data) %in% new_cols] <- (
    marker_names[match(colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data)[colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data) %in% new_cols], names(marker_names))])
  
  # selres <- "SCT_snn_res.0.9"
  top_markers_outer_list <- list()
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  for (selres in res_vector){
    seu.integrated@meta.data$seurat_clusters <- seu.integrated@meta.data[[selres]]
    Idents(seu.integrated) <- selres
    # checks:
    cluster_sample_table <- table(
      #Cluster = Idents(seu.integrated),
      Cluster = seu.integrated@meta.data$seurat_clusters,
      Sample  = seu.integrated$sample.names
    )
    # print(cluster_sample_table)
    cluster_sample_prop <- prop.table(cluster_sample_table, margin = 2)
    # print(round(cluster_sample_prop, 3))
    # tidy version for exporting
    cluster_sample_df <- as.data.frame(cluster_sample_table) %>%
      group_by(Sample) %>%
      mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))
    
    # visualize:
    p <- ggplot(cluster_sample_df,
                aes(x = Sample, y = Prop, fill = Cluster)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
      labs(
        x = NULL,
        y = "Proportion of cells",
        fill = "Cluster"
      ) +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm")
      )
    plot(p)
    outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("cluster_proportions_", selres, "_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
    ggsave(outfig, plot=p, width=8, height=6)
  
    # to plot van-Haver markers:
    # add hulls
    my_hulls <- get_glasswork_layers(
          seu.integrated, 
          clusvar = "seurat_clusters",
          concavity = 3,         # Slightly higher concavity follows the dense core better
          core_quantile = 0.75   # This ignores the 25% most isolated cells
        )
    
    my_hulls_outline <- get_glasswork_layers_outline(
      seu.integrated, 
      clusvar = "seurat_clusters",
      concavity = 3,         # Slightly higher concavity follows the dense core better
      core_quantile = 0.75   # This ignores the 25% most isolated cells
    )
    
    # 2. Add them to your plot
    # I recommend setting alpha low on the points so the Hulls "pop"
    p <- DimPlot(
      seu.integrated, ncol=2,
      reduction = "umap",
      group.by  = "sample.names",
      split.by  = "sample.names",
      pt.size   = 0.1) +
      my_hulls +
      NoLegend() +
      theme_void()
    plot(p)
    
    outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("clusters_samples_", ct, "_res_", selres, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
    ggsave(outfig, plot=p, width=15, height=10)


   # Van-Haver markers - ensure genes are present
   marker_list_filtered <- lapply(marker_list, function(genes) {
      genes[genes %in% rownames(seu.integrated)]
    })
    
    # # subtracting the average expression of "control genes" from the feature genes - needs to be done once only
    # seu.integrated <- AddModuleScore(
    #   seu.integrated,
    #   features = marker_list_filtered,
    #   name     = names(marker_list_filtered),
    #   nbin     = 10
    # )
    
    # # add nice metadata columns (names of the marker_list_filtered list plus a "1" suffix)
    # new_cols <- grep(paste0("(", paste(names(marker_list_filtered), collapse="|"), ")\\d+"), 
    #              colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data), value = TRUE)
    # marker_names <- gsub("\\d+$", "", new_cols)
    # names(marker_names) <- new_cols
    # colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data)[colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data) %in% new_cols] <- (
    #   marker_names[match(colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data)[colnames(seu.integrated@meta.data) %in% new_cols], names(marker_names))])
    
    pp <- list()
    for (marker_name in marker_names){
      pp[[marker_name]] <- FeaturePlot(
        seu.integrated, 
        label=T, label.size = 7,
        features  = marker_name,
        reduction = "umap",
        min.cutoff = "q05",
        max.cutoff = "q95"
      ) +
        my_hulls_outline +
        scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1) +
        NoLegend() +
        theme_void()
    }
    p_combined <- pp[[1]] + pp[[2]] + pp[[3]] + pp[[4]] + pp[[5]] + pp[[6]]
    
    # Define the layout: 
    layout <- "ABC
               DEF"
    
    p_final <- p_combined + 
      plot_layout(design = layout)
    
    plot(p_final)
    outfig <- file.path(Figures, paste("clusters_vanHaver_markers_", ct, "_res_", selres, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep=""))
    ggsave(outfig, plot=p_final, width=15, height=10)
    
    
    
    # marker detection - TO TEST - use "SCT"
    DefaultAssay(seu.integrated) <- "RNA"
    
    markers <- FindAllMarkers(
      seu.integrated,
      only.pos = TRUE,
      test.use = "wilcox",
      logfc.threshold = 0.25,
      min.pct = 0.1
    )
    
    top_markers <- markers %>%
      group_by(cluster) %>%
      slice_max(order_by = avg_log2FC, n = 20)
    
    # for now, filter by patterns; TO DO - filter by the gtf file!
    top_markers_clean <- markers %>%
      filter(!grepl("^ENSG|^LINC|\\-AS[0-9]$|^MIR|^SNHG", gene)) %>% 
      group_by(cluster) %>%
      slice_max(order_by = avg_log2FC, n = 50)
    
    # create a list for the dotplot
    top_markers_list <- list()
    for (cl in unique(top_markers_clean$cluster)){
      top_markers_list[[cl]] <- top_markers_clean$gene[top_markers_clean$cluster==cl]
    }
  
    gene_all <- c()
    top_markers_flat <- top_markers_list
    for (mname in names(top_markers_flat)){
      top_markers_flat[[mname]] <- setdiff(top_markers_flat[[mname]], gene_all)
      gene_all <- union(gene_all, top_markers_flat[[mname]])
    }
  
    p_dot <- DotPlot(
      seu.integrated,
      features = top_markers_flat, # Passing the list creates grouped labels
      cols = c("lightgrey", "red"),
      col.min = 0,
      dot.scale = 6,
      assay = "SCT"
    ) + RotatedAxis() + ggtitle("Top Markers")+
      theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
    plot(p_dot)
    
    ggsave(file.path(Figures, paste("Top_Markers_DotPlot_", ct, "_selres_", 
              selres, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".pdf", sep="")), p_dot, 
           width = length(top_markers_list)*5.5, height = 6, limitsize = FALSE)
  
    # write markers to file
      # save top_markers_list
    max_len <- max(sapply(top_markers_list, length))
    padded_list <- lapply(top_markers_list, function(x) {
      length(x) <- max_len
      return(x)}
      ) # 2. Pad shorter lists with NA so they all match max_len
    padded_df <- as.data.frame(padded_list) # now there will be column names
    colnames(padded_df) <- gsub("X", "Cluster_", colnames(padded_df))
    top_markers_outer_list[[selres]] <- padded_df
  
    # 2. Add a new sheet for EACH resolution inside the loop
    # Clean the name (Excel sheets can't have certain characters or be too long)
    sheet_name <- substr(gsub("[^[:alnum:]]", "_", selres), 1, 31) 
    addWorksheet(wb, sheetName = sheet_name)
    writeData(wb, sheet = sheet_name, x = padded_df)
    #
  

  } # loop for selres
  # 3. Save the final workbook
  saveWorkbook(wb, file.path(Results, paste("Top_Markers_By_Sample_", ct, "_all_nHVG", nHVG_str, ".xlsx", sep="")), overwrite = TRUE)

} # loop for celltype
```
